clue.text: Brought into bright focus with a beacon

definitions.meaning: made to stand out vividly, given prominence
a beacon is a lamp set up on high, so something lit by one is lit from on high

explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise something is to throw light on it; the second reading treats the word as high plus lit.

clue.text: Live only to put the laundry to dry

definitions.meaning: to live somewhere is to reside or frequent it, informally

definitions.text: to put the laundry to dry
definitions.meaning: washing is pegged on a line outdoors to dry

explanation.surface: Someone whose sole purpose in life is drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to reside or loiter somewhere and to peg washing on a line.

clue.text: Bony and emaciated son of Edward III

definitions.meaning: thin, haggard and skeletal
John of ..., Duke of Lancaster, was a son of the English king Edward III

explanation.surface: A description of a thin medieval prince.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means haggard and thin; the name is the English place-name title of John, Duke of Lancaster.

clue.text: Referring to a reference book for astronomical observation

definitions.meaning: consulting a dictionary or directory to find an entry
gazing skyward at the stars

explanation.surface: Checking a star atlas while out stargazing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both finding an entry in a book and raising one's eyes skyward.

clue.text: Harp for a character like Harpo?

definitions.meaning: to harp is to talk on and on about the same subject
Harpo Marx was a comic clown, a silly fellow

explanation.definitionFit: To harp is to keep on talking; a zany clown like Harpo Marx is a silly fool, written as one word.

clue.text: Ain't Tory disposed to be a little loco?

indicators.note: the letters are set out or arranged in a fresh order, as things disposed are laid out

explanation.surface: Asking whether a non-Conservative is inclined to be slightly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loco' looks like slang for mad, but here it is short for locomotive; the question mark marks the plaything as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature model locomotive is a plaything engine, so a small loco.

clue.text: Bread ought to include it

indicators.note: the two words are said to contain the item sought, so it lies within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A baker insisting that loaves contain a certain ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden across the join of the first two words; and as a whole the clue is true, since a loaf is baked from this mixture, while bread is also slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf is baked from a kneaded flour mixture, and both words are slang for money.

clue.text: Read Latin but attached to S American state

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
sed is the Latin word for but

explanation.surface: A Latin scholar mentions a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to have looked through a text carefully.

clue.text: Shattered by the cold presumably

definitions.meaning: broken into fragments
trembled because of the chill

explanation.surface: Something broken apart by frost.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both broke into splinters and trembled with chill.

clue.text: A brainy subject

parts.note: a field of study for clever people, or one that is literally about the brain and nerves

explanation.definitionFit: Medical science of the nervous system, the brain included.

clue.text: He leads you and me to the woman

parts.note: we, in the object case, is us
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A man escorting a couple to a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre or wedding attendant leads guests to their seats.

clue.text: It may finish up in the soup if oil tax is renewed

definitions.text: It may finish up in the soup

indicators.note: renewed means made over in a new form, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh fuel levy may end up getting someone into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' suggests being in trouble, but the bovine tail literally ends up in a soup bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of cattle is a classic soup ingredient.

clue.text: A papist contracted nettle rash in the muniment room

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic, a papist
hives is urticaria, the itchy rash from nettle stings

explanation.surface: A Catholic catching an itchy rash in the record office.
explanation.definitionFit: A muniment room stores title deeds and records, a store of documents.

clue.text: Gully where Rex is caught by a ruffian

indicators.note: the king is held inside the ruffian, as one caught is gripped within

parts.note: a tough is a thug or ruffian
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king seized by a thug in a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A long channel or depression, like a gully.

clue.text: Start blazing away-that's what one hopes it will do

definitions.text: Start blazing away-that's what one hopes it will do

parts.words: Start blazing away-that's what one hopes it will do
parts.note: begin shooting, said of soldiers, while a hearth blaze is hoped to burn brightly

explanation.definitionFit: To begin shooting; a grate blaze in a hearth is also hoped to get going.

clue.text: OED written in code

parts.note: O is a nought or zero, which is a cipher, followed by ED

explanation.surface: A famous dictionary set down in secret writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dictionary's abbreviation splits as O, which is a nought (a cipher), followed by ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Encoded, put into secret writing.

clue.text: Strike and demonstrate for a record programme

parts.note: to hit is to strike
to parade is to show off or display

explanation.surface: Workers striking and marching in protest to set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart show playing best-selling records.

clue.text: Effect caused by a follower with hang up

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
to ring off is to end a phone call

explanation.surface: A result brought about by a disciple and a gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to effect is to accomplish or achieve something.

clue.text: Soft-soled shoes for climbers

definitions.meaning: crepe-soled footwear
plants that climb walls, such as ivy

explanation.surface: Footwear suited to mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for quiet rubber-soled footwear, and climbing plants.

clue.text: Litigation applied to auto body

parts.note: an auto is a car
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about a car's bodywork.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead animal's body, in a variant spelling.

clue.text: Method of surveying sports grounds

definitions.meaning: a technique measuring distance with a graduated rod and telescope
plural of the Latin-derived word for an arena

explanation.surface: How to measure out playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveying technique using a telescope with hairlines; also the plural of arenas for athletics.

clue.text: Design art Lely presented with eyes wide open

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sir Peter Lely painting portraits wide awake.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter Lely was a seventeenth-century court portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchfully, in a wide-awake manner.

clue.text: Umpire employing phrase "Not out in answer to appeal

definitions.text: Not out in answer to appeal

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
using means employing

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire turning down an appeal for a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire, who says 'not out' to turn them down.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining a request, saying no.

clue.text: We'd support it even though all cut up

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath and holds up the first

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it
taken as wed, married

explanation.surface: Backing a plan despite everyone being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: having cut with a saw.

clue.text: Manage to get the feel of things

definitions.meaning: to cope with or control

definitions.text: to get the feel of things
definitions.meaning: to touch or feel with the hands

explanation.surface: A manager learning the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to cope with and to touch with the hands.

clue.text: Find how to clear weeds

definitions.meaning: to discover or unearth information
uproot plants with a spade

explanation.surface: Gardening tips on weeding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both discover and excavate from soil.

clue.text: German flower with a pronounced fragrance

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for fragrance is heard rather than seen

parts.note: an odour is a smell or fragrance

explanation.surface: A strongly scented bloom from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a thing that flows, a river: this one runs along Germany's border with Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and this one forms part of Germany's eastern border.

clue.text: Gunners retreating before skirmish get an old projectile…

indicators.note: going backwards, so the gunners' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a row is a fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: Artillerymen falling back before a fight, getting hit by an ancient missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman's shaft, a missile from before guns.

clue.text: … straight from a barrel

parts.note: beer drawn directly from the cask rather than bottled, following the barrel of a gun in the previous clue

explanation.definitionFit: Beer served from a cask is drawn by tap rather than bottled.

clue.text: Submitted to wages being paid on demobilisation

parts.note: deferred to means submitted or yielded to
pay means wages

explanation.surface: Soldiers accepting their final pay packet as they leave the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Money held back until a serviceman's discharge from the forces.
